maes_1.why: Simultaneous equations are fundamental to algebra; confidence stems from practice and familiarity with systems of linear equations.

maes_2.why: Decimals are straightforward once the basics of fractions are understood; most students grasp decimal operations quickly.

maes_3.why: Determining angles requires knowledge of geometric properties and angle relationships, which can be challenging for some.

maes_4.why: Algebra problems are manageable with a good grasp of variables and operations; most students find them less intimidating than other math topics.

maes_5.why: Trigonometry introduces angles and trigonometric functions, which can be abstract and difficult for beginners to visualize.

maes_6.why: Calculating area and volume involves geometry and spatial reasoning; while not the hardest, it requires understanding formulas.

maes_7.why: Sketching curves demands an intuitive sense of graph behavior and function properties, which can be tricky for those less practiced in graphical analysis.

maes_8.why: Fractions are a core concept easily mastered through repetition; most students achieve high comfort levels with them.

maes_9.why: Finding missing side lengths involves applying the Pythagorean theorem and understanding ratios, which can be less intuitive for some.
